title: Chequit
summary: Chequit is a Shelter Island placename for a point of land at Shelter Island Heights, later associated with Prospect, where the Shelter Island Heights Association developed a hotel and cottages.
address_label: Chequit Point / Shelter Island Heights, Shelter Island, NY
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Manhansett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Chequit preserves a Shelter Island point name whose translation remains uncertain and should not be forced into a weakfish explanation. That uncertainty matters because public history can respect Native language without pretending every surviving name has a simple English equivalent. The general Chequit Point location keeps Shelter Island's coastal geography connected to Indigenous Long Island memory while leaving room for what the records do not securely explain.
history_content: The name preserves a point in the Manhansett/Shelter Island landscape and its later Shelter Island Heights development context. The existing polygon is a modern outline for Chequit Point, not a reconstructed historic boundary.
translation_content:
The surviving entry does not give a secure translation. An editorial note in the source cautions that Chequit should not be confidently treated as a corruption of squeteague, a name associated with weakfish.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names encompass our relationship with the land.”

— Aaron Leggett, Indigenous Place Names Project (n.d.), project statement
whereintheworld_content: Chequit shows how a Native placename remained attached to a visible Shelter Island point even as the area became part of a resort landscape. The fish-name explanation remains uncertain and should be read carefully.
